entry.title: I want to build a house with you, tell me it's a whole life too
entry.summary:
Author: Lacerta26

Rating: ExplicitLanguage: EnglishWords: 17,405Chapters: 3/4Kudos: 95

Summary: Buck didn't think he'd end up back at Eddie's after everything. All the things that drove him here haven't changed and neither have the things that made him leave again. Thirty four years old and able to drop everything in his life because he had no dependents, no responsibilities, no ties. Chris was gone and Eddie was following him and Buck was only at South Bedford because he was being left behind. Buck has reckoned with his feelings by now, this past year after Bobby, after everything that went on in the desert, the lengths Eddie went to, bringing things into sharper focus. He's in love with Eddie, has been in love with Eddie for so long it just became part of the fabric of the universe, the baseline from which Buck operates. He's made his peace with it too, aware that Eddie doesn't feel the same. He'd do anything for Eddie and Chris but he felt more like a guest than he ever had when they came back to LA, sleeping on their couch, waiting to be asked to leave. Better to go than be pushed, he figured, and yet the path always seems to lead back to here. So, South Bedford it is, only there are four of them now, not three because Buck is responsible for more than himself these days.

Summary: Buck swallowed; his throat went tight. His throat stung, and his eyes had a sharp, lingering pain. Eddie sighed. “I feel like I started realizing the way I was dismissing you once Christopher pointed it out. He told me he noticed me pushing you away, and it made him sad for you. Summary: Chimney didn’t think he’d ever get used to calling it ‘his office’, even though it had been a few months already since he’d stepped into the impossibly large captain’s shoes. As he passed by the plaque fixed on the wall just outside the office door, he reached up and touched the cold metal right next to where the name was etched and bowed his head in a nod of respect to his predecessor, as he had at the start of every shift since it had been screwed into place. He wondered, if he kept doing this every day, how long it would take that spot to begin to change colour. And whether it would take equally as long for these feelings to fade. Or would it remain this way for the decades it would take to wear it down the metal to reveal the wooden mount underneath.
